title: Clear from the right, serve from the left
instruction: Clear the guest's starter plate onto the bus tray and serve the main course. House standard: clear from the guest's right, serve food from the guest's left.
context: The instruction gives the house standard of table service. Restaurantware's fine-dining tips for servers: serve from the left, clear from the right; WebstaurantStore's guide: always clear from the guest's right (the serving side varies by house); Tonno restaurant's server training: pre-plated courses served from the left, cleared from the right. The guest faces the robot, so the guest's right is the robot's left: the robot must map the guest's sides onto its own frame. One rule is unstated: the new plate is never set down before the used one has gone (doing so scores 0). The natural way is the left arm clearing toward the guest's right while the right arm serves from the guest's left, at the same time, as two servers would. One arm could do both in turn, so two arms are natural, not required. Done by: waiters, bussers, banquet and catering servers.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); heights above the table; sizes x by y by height. The guest (visual only: a blue-grey block 18 x 34 x 40 cm, centred at x 62, y 0) sits facing the robot, so the guest's right is the robot's left (+y) and the guest's left is the robot's right (-y). Cover (the guest's place setting): a brown placemat 26 x 26 cm, 1 mm thick (visual only), centred at x 36, y 0. Starter plate: 0.25 kg, porcelain, square, 20 x 20 cm: a 1 cm base with a raised rim lip 1.2 cm wide and 1.5 cm high round its edge (2.5 cm tall in all), on the placemat at x 36, y 0, with crumbs on it (visual, 5 x 4 x 0.6 cm). Pass: a fixed grey shelf 22 x 24 x 4 cm, centred at x 14, y 0. Main course plate: 0.30 kg, the same plate, on the pass at x 14, y 0, with a steak 5 x 7.5 x 2.5 cm centred 4.5 cm from the plate's centre toward the guest, and mash (4.5 x 5 x 3 cm, on the left) and greens (4 x 4.5 x 2 cm, on the right) centred 4 cm from the plate's centre toward the robot (the food is visual only). Bus tray: fixed, dark grey, 24 x 24 cm with a rim 1.5 cm high (floor and walls 0.6 cm thick), centred at x 20, y 30, on the robot's left (the guest's right).
scoring: Every step, from poses; the score at the end counts. A plate's path is its centre's horizontal position at every step from the first step its underside is more than 1 cm above its starting height. The side is judged where the path crosses the circle 10 cm round the cover's centre (interpolated between steps): the starter is cleared from the guest's right if its path first leaves the circle at least 5 cm to the robot's left (+y) of the cover's centre, and the main is served from the guest's left if its path last enters the circle at least 5 cm to the robot's right (-y), that is within 60 degrees of that side; a plate never lifted has no side. Placed: the starter rests on the bus tray (its centre within 7 cm of the tray's centre along x and along y, its underside within 1.2 cm of the table) and the main is down on the cover (its underside within 4 mm of the table, its centre within 3 cm of the cover's centre), no finger pad within 8 mm of either plate, and both plates moving less than 2 mm over 1 s. If placed: 1.0 with both sides right, 0.5 with one side wrong, 0.25 with both wrong; minus 0.25 (not below 0) if the steak points more than 25 degrees away from the guest (+x), seen from above. 0 otherwise, and 0 from the moment the main is down on the table (underside within 4 mm) within 8 cm of the cover's centre before the starter's centre has been 20 cm from it, the main is left resting on the starter (their centres within 8 cm horizontally, the main's underside above the starter's and at most 2.5 cm above it, no finger pad within 2 cm of the main), either plate's centre passes beyond x 50 cm (over the guest's lap), a finger pad comes within 8 mm of the main course's food (a zone 13 x 13 x 4 cm over the plate's centre, from the top of its base up), or a plate is dropped (it falls 3 cm within 0.5 s with no finger pad within 2 cm of it). Success: 1.0.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Put the starter plate back on the placemat at the cover and the main course plate back on the pass, steak toward the guest.
fidelity: Rigid boxes: each plate is a base and four rim lips; the pass and bus tray are fixed. Contacts and friction are simulated. The food is visual and fixed; an 8 mm finger keep-out over the main plate stands in for it. The guest is a static block; the line x 50 cm, which no plate's centre may cross, stands in for the lap. The arms face the guest across the table, so the serving side is the plate's path: the side on which it crosses a 10 cm circle round the cover, at least 5 cm to that side.
